record.paper_title: Descriptions of Cantor Sets: A Set-Theoretic Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Find an explicit set-theoretic formula or a recursive set-theoretic formula for deterministic Cantor subsets of [0,1] that are generated by an iterated-function system with K ≥ 2 maps and that do not preserve bilateral symmetry.

evidence.quote: The preceding survey has shown that three natural families of deterministic Cantor sets—two of measure zero with explicit descriptions and one of non–negative measure defined recursively—share a common symmetric architecture and possess rational construction end-points; indeed, the classical middle-third Cantor set lies in the intersection of all three.

(OP1) Asymmetric constructions. Devise explicit or recursive set-theoretic formulas for Cantor sets generated by iterated-function systems (IFS) with K ≥ 2 maps that do not preserve bilateral symmetry.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K ≥ 2 be an integer and let Φ = {φ_1, …, φ_K} be an iterated function system on the unit interval [0,1], where each φ_i : [0,1] → [0,1] is a contraction (for concreteness, an affine contraction φ_i(x) = r_i x + t_i with 0 < r_i < 1 and 0 ≤ t_i ≤ 1 − r_i) chosen so that the images φ_i([0,1]) are pairwise disjoint or meet only at endpoints. Let C(Φ) ⊆ [0,1] denote the unique nonempty compact set satisfying

  C(Φ) = ⋃_{i=1}^{K} φ_i(C(Φ)).

Say that Φ (or C(Φ)) is bilaterally symmetric if C(Φ) is invariant under the reflection x ↦ 1 − x; otherwise call Φ asymmetric.

Problem. For asymmetric iterated function systems Φ of the above form with K ≥ 2 maps, provide an explicit closed-form set-theoretic description, or alternatively an explicit recursive set-theoretic description, of the attractor C(Φ) ⊆ [0,1] — that is, a formula expressing C(Φ) directly in terms of the parameters {(r_i, t_i)}_{i=1}^{K} using elementary set-theoretic operations (unions, intersections, complements, arithmetic operations on intervals) rather than only as the fixed point of the Hutchinson operator.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem (OP1) in a 2025 survey on set-theoretic descriptions of Cantor sets. No published resolution providing such explicit/recursive set-theoretic formulas for asymmetric IFS Cantor sets was located.
